title: The Ship Found Sailing Across the Ocean With Nobody Aboard
logline: In 1872, a merchant ship was discovered drifting across the Atlantic with its cargo intact but all ten people aboard missing.
narration: A ship was found drifting across the Atlantic Ocean. Its cargo was still there. Food and water remained on board. But every person had vanished. The ship was called the Mary Celeste. On November 7, 1872, it left New York for Genoa, Italy, carrying ten people, including the captain, his wife and their two-year-old daughter. Almost a month later, another ship spotted it near the Azores. Sailors approached and climbed aboard. What they discovered was extraordinary. The ship was still seaworthy. Its cargo of industrial alcohol was largely intact. Personal belongings remained in the cabins. But there was nobody anywhere on board. Even the lifeboat was missing. The captain, his family and all seven crew members were never found. Investigators examined the mystery, but no explanation was ever proven. More than 150 years later, one question remains: why did ten people abandon a ship that was still floating?
note: Narration and scene captions are Nandu's exact words. Tags, extra shots and staging notes are Claude's plan; every addition is marked ADDED or CHANGED.

scenes.caption: A ship was found drifting across the Atlantic Ocean. Its cargo was still there. Food and water remained on board. But every person had vanished.

shots.must_see: Wide: a lonely wooden two-masted ship drifting on a grey ocean, nobody on deck
shots.staging: ADDED: grey flat sea to the horizon, low cloud, a thin wake; no gulls (animals are not built)

shots.must_see: Close: the ship's cargo, rows of barrels lashed on the deck
shots.staging: ADDED: ropes and canvas on the barrels so it reads as cargo

shots.must_see: Close: a table on deck with bread and a water cask, no hand reaching for it
shots.staging: ADDED: bread loaf, tin mug, water cask (the narration says food and water)

scenes.caption: The ship was called the Mary Celeste. On November 7, 1872, it left New York for Genoa, Italy, carrying ten people, including the captain, his wife and their two-year-old daughter.

shots.must_see: Wide: New York harbor wharf with warehouses, the ship tied up, barrels piled on the quay
shots.staging: ADDED: stone wharf, 3 brick warehouses, mast poles of other ships far back; sky day

shots.must_see: Medium: seven sailors in a row on the quay and gangway, the ten people counted by eye
shots.staging: ADDED: 7 crew cards in blue shirts, 3 outfit variants; the narration says ten people, so the crowd is the ten

shots.must_see: Medium: the captain, his wife and their small daughter standing together on the deck (left to right: captain, wife, daughter)
shots.staging: ADDED: the girl is a small card; same outfits as later scenes

scenes.caption: Almost a month later, another ship spotted it near the Azores. Sailors approached and climbed aboard.

shots.staging: ADDED: different sail colour on the Dei Gratia so the two ships are never confused; Dei Gratia always on the left

shots.must_see: Medium: one sailor on the Dei Gratia deck pointing at the distant ship, a second sailor beside him
shots.staging: ADDED: the Azores are not drawn (no island); the narration only needs the distance

shots.must_see: Medium: a rowboat with three sailors alongside the Mary Celeste hull, already arrived
shots.staging: CHANGED vs the draft: shows the boat arrived, not rowing (rowing is a hard action; hard cut instead)

shots.staging: CHANGED vs the draft: standing on deck, not climbing the railing (climbing is a hard action)

shots.must_see: Medium: a sailor taps the wheel and the mast, the ship upright and firm
shots.staging: ADDED: shows 'still seaworthy' as an intact mast and wheel, no damage

shots.must_see: Close: the open cargo hatch with rows of sealed barrels below, dim light
shots.staging: ADDED: dark box under the hatch, barrels in 3 rows

shots.must_see: Close: the table with plates and a tin cup, a chair pushed back

shots.must_see: Wide: the deserted ship on endless grey sea, nobody on deck

from my own knowledge, to be confirmed a: Mary Celeste, brigantine, left New York for Genoa Nov 7, 1872 (as in the script)
10 aboard: Captain Benjamin Briggs, wife Sarah, daughter Sophia (2), 7 crew
found by the Dei Gratia near the Azores, early December 1872
cargo industrial alcohol, mostly intact; lifeboat missing; no proven explanation

staging_notes.ten_people: The narration says ten people. The crowd shot in c2 shows the captain, wife, daughter and seven crew as cards.
staging_notes.sides: Dei Gratia always on the left, Mary Celeste on the right. Captain left, wife centre, daughter right.
staging_notes.hard_actions_removed: Rowing and climbing are shown as arrived/standing; hard cuts carry the action.
staging_notes.invented_details: Doll in the cabin, bread and cup on the deck table, map shapes: small props that carry 'belongings' and 'food and water'. No new story facts.
